transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-10
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood Infra), Sara Patel (Beacon ML), Tom Reynolds (Beacon Head ML), Ibrahim Q. (SRE), Emily Cho (Product)

Summary:
Quick review of week 3: perf deltas between INT8/FP8, quality regressions flagged, triage of 12 regression cases, agreement on targeted tuning and on-prem run next week.

Topics:
- baseline (FP16) metrics recap
- INT8 perf & quality tradeoffs
- FP8 experimental run and observed deltas
- failure-case triage and prompt-level debugging
- rollout plan and canary thresholds

Action items (quick): see metadata action_items.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Alex Kim: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um let's kick off, quick agenda-- results, triage, next steps.
[00:00:18] Sara Patel: cool, yes thank you. we got the week 2 pack and ran those 2.4k prompts against the baseline and int8/FP8 variants.
[00:00:27] Priya Rao: quick note, the run used our caching off-path first, so the numbers lean a bit conservative on latency; Marcus patched the KV emission afterwards.
[00:00:36] Marcus Li: yeah i turned on KV cache metrics after the first batch; there's a header in the logs where you'll see cache-hit ratio per shard.
[00:00:44] Tom Reynolds: can we start with the headline perf numbers? what should we expect if we flip to INT8 or FP8 in production?
[00:00:52] Priya Rao: baseline FP16 avg p50 latency 410ms on 2k seq, throughput ~140 tokens/sec sustained. INT8 gave ~28% lower p50 (so ~295ms) and throughput +1.6x. FP8 showed ~36-42% latency drop depending on seq distribution and hit throughput ~1.9x. those are median numbers, there's tail variability.
[00:01:12] Emily Cho: that sounds great, the cost delta is important — how did that map to estimated token $/k?
[00:01:20] Alex Kim: ballpark: at current reserved rates INT8 is ~38% unit-cost reduction vs FP16; FP8 about ~52% reduction. we'll attach the cost model spreadsheet.
[00:01:30] Ibrahim Q.: nice — quality? numbers trended acceptable but we flagged regressions?
[00:01:36] Priya Rao: yes so summary: INT8 has small semantic deltas, we measured semantic-sim similarity drop of median 0.004 (on embedding sim) and a 1.6% drop in exact-match on the QA set. FP8 had larger variance — median sim drop ~0.012 and exact-match down 3.8% overall, but it depended heavily on prompt length and certain token distributions.
[00:01:57] Sara Patel: do you have examples of the worst failures? we saw a few hallucinations in FP8 where the model confidently invented dates.
[00:02:06] Priya Rao: yes we pulled 12 failure cases — most are in FP8, a handful in INT8. typical pattern: long context (> 2.5k tokens) + lots of numeric tables + prompt with several constraints. FP8 sometimes drops subtle negation signals.
[00:02:24] Tom Reynolds: okay, how reproducible are these— are they deterministic?
[00:02:29] Marcus Li: determinism is good for model-only runs; when batching and async IO are added, there's some interleaving that can flip a case. we isolated a couple nondet cases where seeding + kv-cache state made the output diverge.
[00:02:43] Priya Rao: important operational note: INT8 path uses a different kernel that doesn't yet support fused rotary in all sharding modes — that contributed to two regression signatures; FP8 uses a lower-precision matmul kernel that amplifies small weights differences.
[00:03:01] Alex Kim: let's walk through the triage list. Sara, you flagged the top 5 highest-severity prompts, right?
[00:03:07] Sara Patel: yes, we prioritized 5 that matter to clinical summarization; I've annotated them in the spreadsheet with severity and expected output. link: (redwood/benchmarks/bht-week3.xlsx).
[00:03:18] Priya Rao: ok for those five, our plan: 1) run per-layer qscale experiments, 2) try per-token temp-scaling and prompt rewrite fallback, 3) run an FP16 oracle on just those prompts under identical batching to separate model variance from runtime issues.
[00:03:33] Ibrahim Q.: what about fallback in prod — can we route those types of prompts to FP16 automatically?
[00:03:38] Alex Kim: yes, Redwood routing policy supports per-route fallback; you can mark route metadata and set threshold (e.g., semantic-sim < 0.92 triggers fallback). we'll send a sample policy.
[00:03:49] Tom Reynolds: two operational asks — can we do a canary where 5% of requests hit INT8 for two days and capture per-token diff logs? and we want to know the SLO impact.
[00:03:58] Marcus Li: provisioning-wise we can simulate canary load easily on a dedicated pool; need to confirm expected throughput. Marcus: i'll provision a 4-node pool for the on-prem run on the 19th.
[00:04:08] Sara Patel: what about the KV cache — earlier you said cache was off for first run, re-run with cache will change latency a lot right?
[00:04:13] Priya Rao: absolutely — with prefix cache warm, median latency for INT8 drops another ~30ms and throughput bump ~8-12%. we included cold/warm metrics in the spreadsheet.
[00:04:25] Emily Cho: is there a known class of prompts that are safe to immediately move to INT8? we have a high-volume diagnostic API that could benefit.
[00:04:32] Priya Rao: short-answer: Q/A with short context (<=512 tokens) and non-numeric summarization tasks are low risk on INT8. long docs and numeric transforms are higher risk.
[00:04:45] Tom Reynolds: curious — any differences by top-p/temperature tuning?
[00:04:50] Priya Rao: yes, higher temp amplifies fp quant noise; so FP8 at temp 0.9 had more variance than at 0.2. for deterministic tasks we recommend sticking to temp <=0.2 on reduced-precision models.
[00:05:02] Alex Kim: ok let's sketch the experiment plan and timeline now. Week 1 (this week) — run per-layer qscale grid on the 5 severity prompts, run 5k prompt A/B at 1% traffic to collect sampling. Week 2 — on-prem 4-node run and canary 5% production routing for 48h. Week 3 — review and decide rollout thresholds.
[00:05:20] Sara Patel: are there any quick mitigations we can deploy if FP8 shows unacceptable drift?
[00:05:24] Priya Rao: yes, immediate mitigations: 1) route high-risk routes to FP16, 2) use INT8 instead of FP8 for those routes, 3) apply prompt-level bias-correction (we can auto-rewrite prompts for negation).
[00:05:36] Ibrahim Q.: logging volume for per-token diffs will be huge — who stores it?
[00:05:40] Alex Kim: Redwood can stream diffs to your S3 bucket or to our long-term analytics if you opt-in; we'll provide a cost estimate.
[00:05:47] Tom Reynolds: ok let's call out specific metrics we want in the canary dashboard.
[00:05:51] Priya Rao: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, semantic-sim median & 95th, exact-match for QA sets, hallucination-count (heuristic), cache-hit ratio, concurrency per shard, and error rate.
[00:06:07] Emily Cho: make sure to include cost per 1M tokens so we can compare with our budget line-item.
[00:06:11] Alex Kim: yep will include that.
[00:06:16] Sara Patel: quick question on calibration — do you recommend per-layer scale or per-channel?
[00:06:20] Priya Rao: per-layer is our default fast sweep; per-channel gets better quality but is heavier; for the 5 priority prompts we'll try per-layer first and then the top 2 layers per-channel if needed.
[00:06:34] Tom Reynolds: any red flags about our infra? Ibrahim?
[00:06:38] Ibrahim Q.: network is good, but our on-prem has mixed gen GPUs; we should mirror Redwood's kernel selection, otherwise perf numbers will differ. Marcus: please document required CUDA/cuDNN and kernel versions.
[00:06:49] Marcus Li: will do, i'll attach an install matrix and exact kernel build used in the test.
[00:06:55] Alex Kim: ok, let's record the regression triage notes: PRI 1 (3 cases) - clinical date hallucinations (FP8). PRI 2 (4 cases) - negation flip (INT8+FP8). PRI 3 (5 cases) - formatting/noise (mostly FP8). full list in sheet.
[00:07:13] Sara Patel: i added expected acceptability threshold — we require no more than 1% critical regressions on the top-100 clinical prompts to go to production.
[00:07:22] Priya Rao: noted. we'll prioritize to make sure that metric is met in canary.
[00:07:27] Alex Kim: anything else on tuning?
[00:07:30] Emily Cho: I'm worried about edge-case privacy — if we change kernels or quantization, does anything change in our audit logs or encryption?
[00:07:37] Alex Kim: no change to audit logging; data at rest/encryption stays the same. only difference is compute path. for Private deployment we'll integrate KMS/HSM as before.
[00:07:48] Ibrahim Q.: also want SAML SSO test plan for on-prem console access, we will need RBAC roles.
[00:07:54] Alex Kim: we'll send our SSO integration guide and an example role mapping.
[00:07:59] Tom Reynolds: ok, let's finish with a quick recap and owners.
[00:08:03] Alex Kim: recap — Redwood to share consolidated perf spreadsheet, raw logs, canary policy doc; customer to provide priority prompts and label set; infra to provision on-prem cluster for 19th run. owners and dates in action items.
[00:08:20] Sara Patel: thanks all.
[00:08:22] Priya Rao: thanks, bye.

(remaining ~37m was Q/A and detailed triage where Priya walked through individual failures; transcript excerpts:)
[00:12:05] Priya Rao: case 4 — FP8 produced an extra sentence "on March 12th" where baseline omitted date; we traced to quantization noise causing beam re-ranking shift.
[00:17:40] Priya Rao: we re-ran case 7 with per-layer scale 0.92 on layer 22 and it recovered the expected constraint token in 3/3 runs; candidate mitigation.
[00:24:12] Marcus Li: perf note — when we enable kernel-level fused attention the INT8 p95 tail reduces significantly; we left it off in the first runs to keep parity.
[00:31:01] Alex Kim: final note — if FP8 quality after tuning remains borderline, best path is to use INT8 in prod as mid-point; FP8 optimal for very high-volume non-safety-critical workflows.
